set.body:
Split out of the sweep parent bd-01M1697234KP2X44X6Q8S6C6Y7 at its closure, so it is not buried
in a closed record. Full analysis: post-01M16V4C7C0HH67N46BHHXXQY5.

THE FIRST SWEEP IS DONE and it covered types that TRIED to be construction boundaries and were
defeated by Mirror.fromProduct -- private-constructor case classes. It cannot find a type with NO
boundary, because there is no privacy to defeat, and tightening its criterion pushes such a type
further out of view.

SECOND POPULATION, greppable: a validator whose return type is its OWN argument type, on a type
that is publicly constructible. `def validated(g: X): ValidatedNec[DomainError, X]` says, in the
type system's own words, "I checked this and I have no way to tell you" -- nothing downstream can
distinguish a checked value from an unchecked one, and copy() on a validated instance silently
produces an unvalidated one.

MEASURED: 13 validators wear the signature. Of the nine types resolved, EIGHT are public case
classes:
  TranscriptAtlas        core/transcript.scala:81
  SurfaceAtlas           core/atlas.scala:159
  LatePoolingRecipe      embed-core/identity.scala:186
  SidecarManifest        features/sidecar.scala:44
  FeatureDerivation      features/derivation.scala:147
  InterviewSource        interview/atlas.scala:32
  RecallGraph            recall/graph.scala:12   (filed separately, bd-01M16V1QAXR4JT1F174H2BTQT3)
  PromptPackageManifest  acquire/prompt.scala:51

CONTROL: ClaimMeta wears the identical signature and is NOT a defect, because sweep slice 2 gave
it a private constructor. So the screen discriminates rather than flagging every validator in the
repo, and it demonstrates that the fix moves a type from the defective population into the safe
one. Cross-reference against constructibility before filing anything here: for a
private-constructor type, returning its own type is CORRECT, since the validator is then the only
way to obtain one.

Four of the eight are in core and features, the modules everything depends on. FeatureDerivation
is the type the lexical-features decision requires to distinguish a Glasgow row from a glmnet row
by identity, and its own construction is unguarded.

NOT IN SCOPE: acquire/patch.scala:192, `def validate(graph: G): Either[PatchError, G] =
Right(graph)`. Its comment documents the permissive default as deliberate ("Optional whole-graph
validation"). Worth knowing an applier that does not override it performs no whole-graph check,
but that is a design question for PatchApplier's owner.

Slices should follow the first sweep's shape -- per module, independently gateable -- because
this property is per-type like the first one, NOT like the level: Int migration which must be
atomic (see AGENTS.md rule 7).
set.title: sweep 2: validators that return their own input type on publicly-constructible types (8 of 9; core and features worst affected)
